feature: QUIC handshake prepared compression for every server algorithm
decision: prepare zlib, brotli, and zstd Certificate views once per process so the client's offered order cannot fall back to on-demand preparation
head: e2db0c29

workload.tls: QUIC v1, TLS 1.3, pinned P-256 CertificateVerify

conclusion: Preparing only zlib left the default brotli-first client offer to prepare brotli and zstd on demand for every handshake. Preparing all three default server algorithms removes 1,900 allocations and 1,046,700 bytes over 100 handshakes, and lowers p50 from 309.8 us to 191.6 us versus the original on-demand baseline.
